thesis:
One sentence: the world is re-pricing from convenience to security, and from asset-light narrative to physical chokepoints, at a 5% cost of money that is the regime rather than the anomaly. Every recurring observation across the September briefs points the same direction — Meta funding seven gas plants for one data center, Amazon's $8B Generac order, Mitsui contracting LNG explicitly for data centers, Talen/Constellation frameworks, Quanta's raised outlook. Electricity availability, not GPU supply, is the binding constraint on AI, which converts the AI trade from a semiconductor story into a power-industrial story with a decade-long capex channel. Compute and energy are becoming the same asset class; the intermediaries that own electrons, interconnects, turbines, switchgear, skilled trades and memory are the toll roads. The financing structure of the AI buildout is visibly circular (Nvidia into Anthropic, vendor-linked cloud commitments), which tells you the eventual drawdown is a capital-structure event, not a demand event — the electrons get consumed either way.

On the human side, the durable shift is that people are buying time and security rather than intelligence or convenience. The edge-AI query set ('ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service') is consumers outsourcing the lowest-status use of their hours; Copilot at 30M seats is enterprises buying labour substitution. Delegation is also replacing search — Meta's Muse agent, the $1,299 glasses, the standoff with Amazon over agent access — which is the largest re-plumbing of advertising and take-rate economics since mobile, and it is currently unpriced in ad-tech. In health, the 107% surge in robotic-surgery intent spanning hysterectomy, hernia, prostate and knee, plus Medtronic raising guidance on heart devices, says an aging cohort is shopping for restored function, not managed disease; combined with continuous glucose monitoring this makes devices and procedures the volume growth vector while the GLP-1 trade matures into a price war. Security is the other universal: cyber is now a non-discretionary tax on AI adoption (a single attack broke Boston Scientific's guidance), energy self-reliance is a purchased good ('power grid failure' searches alongside Amazon buying generators), and status is migrating from consumption to ownership of scarce physical things — gold, land, energy assets.

The losing side is equally consistent and I would not fight it: levered consumers, marginal housing, mid-tier experiences, and any business whose moat was cheap capital. Housing demand is rationed by monthly payment, not price — 7% mortgages freeze both moves and refis, builders cut price rather than build, and households repair-and-stay-put (HD attention +51%, flagged not-priced; BLDR likewise). That is a maintenance/MRO trade, not a housing-starts trade, and the housing-undersupply theme's trend score of 22 against a narrative of 15 confirms no one is even pretending. Similarly, the consumer is making cash-flow purchases and refusing financed ones, stretching auto loan duration to defend the payment — the signature of late-cycle household stress that shows up in search before it shows up in the data.

For capital allocation over 3-10 years this means: overweight the constraint owners (power generation and flexibility, transmission EPC, mechanical contractors, memory, optics, copper, gas/LNG), overweight the non-discretionary taxes (cybersecurity, custody/wealth platforms, payments rails), overweight health-as-procedure (devices, CGM), and be selective in AI software — own the distribution incumbents and outcome-priced tools, avoid seat-priced software whose unit of value AI deflates (Adobe's soft guide, Wix's cut are the tell). Model Western AI accelerator China revenue toward zero given Huawei's Ascend 960 on a Q1 2027 timetable. Underwrite everything against a permanently higher risk-free rate with $365 trillion of global debt competing at every auction.

theme_ranking.why: The single most repeated, most concretely evidenced shift across every brief: hyperscalers are funding generation directly. Narrative 83 but trend only 34 means the flow hasn't arrived yet — that's the entry, not the disqualifier. Electrons are the constraint for a decade.

Gas is the marginal AI fuel and energy security is now a financial variable ($107 crude, export-ban politics, Mitsui LNG-for-data-centers). Trend 57 with pricing 59 means it is partly in, but the contracted, multi-decade nature of the demand is not.

Transmission EPC, switchgear, turbines and behind-the-meter flexibility are the non-substitutable link between compute demand and power supply. Quanta's raised outlook and Emerald AI validate the headroom problem is real and paid for.

A permanent tax on AI adoption, not a cyclical budget. Boston Scientific's guidance broke on an attack; enterprises are restricting external models over data fear. Pricing 67 is the highest in the set — own it, but pay attention to entry.

Real, self-funding demand, but the financing is circular and China TAM is going to zero. Memory and optics are the tightest links and least exposed to a training pause. Attention 91 with pricing 56 means selectivity, not abstinence.

The clearest unpriced signal in the dataset: attention 94 against pricing 36, explicitly flagged attention_not_priced, with a 107% robotic-surgery intent surge and Medtronic guidance raise behind it. Aging demographics make this volume growth, not a cycle.

Time is what's being bought. But the theme contains both winners (distribution incumbents, outcome-priced tools) and losers (seat-priced suites). Highest trend score at 61; requires security selection, not theme exposure.

24/7 tokenised settlement plus a demographic-scale need for advice, custody and fraud protection. Scaled brokers and custodians win structurally; exchange-hours monopoly value compresses. Narrative 70 already elevated.

Rare-earth leverage confirms supply-chain sovereignty is the long war. Trend 43 and narrative only 34 while pricing is 55 — the market is bored with a multi-decade spend. Skilled-trade contractors are the way to own it.
Fiscal-deficit insurance with $365tn global debt and status migrating from consumption to ownership of scarce physical things. Narrative 71 is already loud, which caps the edge.

Semiconductor sovereignty (Micron Sanand, Nvidia-Australia, Fujitsu Monaka) means fab capex is politically underwritten. But China share loss and the circular financing of AI capex make it more cyclical than the power themes.

Data-center buildout plus grid capex collides with contracting materials flow — a supply-constrained repricing once the macro scare passes. Pricing 57 means partly discounted; trend 51 says the flow hasn't confirmed.

Inference migrating to devices is real and the query evidence is strong, but attention 88 vs trend 49 says narrative is running ahead of the revenue. Margin capture is contested between device OEMs and silicon.
Continuous measurement replacing episodic treatment is a durable behavioural shift, but attention 26 means no catalyst and the 5-20 year horizon poorly matches a 5% discount rate.
Rails benefit from programmable money and multi-currency fragmentation; take-rate risk rises if agents intermediate the transaction layer. Steady, not exciting.
Highest trend at 61 but pricing 59 and narrative 77 — fully appreciated. The incremental margin is migrating to whoever solves power and to on-prem/sovereign deployment.
Order-book status is real (5,000 Optimus units) but consumer humanoids are status purchases and construction robotics will not fix housing this cycle. Pricing 58 already embeds a lot of hope.

The agent-owns-intent hypothesis is the biggest potential re-plumbing since mobile, but it is speculative and the theme scores lowest on attention (18). Asymmetric optionality in specific names rather than theme conviction.
Trading down is happening (Walmart raise, Kroger, Deckers, Next) but narrative 77 vs trend 38 says it's a consensus story with deteriorating fundamentals — margins get competed away.

Real demand, but Novo's rebrand and 'rethinking' amid a GLP-1 price war signal maturation into a share battle. Pricing 61 exceeds trend 60; devices and procedures are the better expression of the same health shift.
Security is the era's premium need, but the theme scores are flat across the board (trend 40, attention 41) and sovereign budget capacity is squeezed by term premium.
Correct direction, wrong clock. Gas is the marginal AI fuel for this decade; nuclear's 5-20 year horizon is badly matched to a 5% risk-free rate and trend 37 confirms no flow.
Mobility is being repriced by fuel and ownership cost, which helps the thesis, but pricing 55 against trend 56 leaves no edge and capital intensity is brutal at 5%.
The in-home consolidation is durable (Visa data) but content economics are deflationary and narrative 58 exceeds trend 50. A share-shift story, not a value-creation story.
Orbital compute is a fascinating inference from the power/latency constraint, but narrative 64 vs attention 38 and a 5-20 year horizon makes it a venture bet in public clothing.
Trend 36 and narrative 41 — a mature theme whose convenience premium is being competed away, and whose take-rate is exactly what agents threaten to disintermediate.
Stablecoin rails matter as plumbing, but trend 33 is among the weakest and the hard-asset demand is going to gold and energy, not tokens.
Demand exists; the operator cannot sell it profitably at $107 crude. Ryanair cutting capacity, NCLH guidance cut, MGM deal collapse. Narrative 25 is honest.
The shortage is real but uninvestable at 7% mortgages: trend 22, narrative 15. The tradeable expression is repair-and-stay-put MRO, not starts or builders.

beneficiary_profiles: Constraint owners: entities that control scarce electrons, interconnect queue positions, gas pipeline capacity, HBM/DRAM supply and copper reserves — pricing power accrues to whoever owns the physically non-replicable link.

Picks-and-shovels for the power-industrial AI complex: turbine, switchgear, generator, transformer and behind-the-meter generation suppliers whose backlog is being funded by hyperscaler balance sheets rather than regulated utility capex.
Skilled-trade aggregators: mechanical/electrical contractors and transmission EPC firms that convert a scarce labour pool into multi-year backlog at rising margin (FIX, PWR profile).
Non-discretionary tax collectors: cybersecurity, identity and fraud-protection vendors whose spend rises mechanically with every unit of AI deployed and every AI-enabled scam.
Toll roads on delegated intent: platforms that hold the consumer's transaction intent when an agent, not a human, does the shopping — the ad and take-rate economics re-concentrate there.
Health-as-procedure suppliers: device, robotic-surgery and continuous-monitoring companies capturing an aging cohort that shops for restored function rather than managed disease.
Scaled custodians and brokers: beneficiaries of 24/7 tokenised settlement, multi-venue/multi-currency access, and a demographic wave of estate, advice and income needs.
Cash-generative short-duration compounders: businesses that clear a permanently 5% hurdle rate on today's free cash flow rather than on terminal-value promises.
Repair-and-stay-put beneficiaries: MRO, home improvement and building-products distribution that monetise a frozen housing turnover market.
Outcome-priced software: vendors that can charge for work done rather than seats occupied, because AI deflates the seat.

not_priced_candidates.why: Pricing 12 — the lowest in the entire universe — with opportunity 61 and gap 32. The market has priced The Trade Desk for terminal disruption by walled gardens, while the actual structural shift (agents intermediating shopping intent) is a 2-5 year speculative war whose outcome is unresolved. An independent demand-side buying layer is optionality the tape is charging nothing for.

Pricing 24 against opportunity 70 and gap 43 — the largest gap in the universe. Sits at the intersection of AI-driven ad targeting and attention economics, two themes where trend (55-61) exceeds pricing (24-36). If delegation re-plumbs advertising, the machine-learning bidding layer is the least substitutable piece.

Pricing 32, gap 25, and separately flagged in attention_not_priced. The consensus is fixated on the circularity of its AI capex commitments; the under-appreciated leg is that sovereign/on-prem deployment demand — accelerated by Nvidia, Palantir and Booz Allen restricting external models — flows toward vendors who will run compute inside a customer's perimeter.

Highest opportunity in the universe at 71 with gap 28 and pricing only 50. Memory is the tightest link in the AI chain and the least exposed to a frontier-model pause because inference and edge deployment consume HBM and DRAM regardless of training cadence. Sanand adds the semiconductor-sovereignty premium. The market still trades it as a cyclical.

Pricing 26, gap 26. The market is applying the 'AI kills seat-priced software' discount to a franchise that actually sells outcomes (a filed return, a paid employee) and owns SMB financial distribution — precisely the incumbent-with-distribution profile that our thesis says wins the agent era rather than loses it.

The cleanest universe expression of the single strongest unpriced theme signal: medical-devices attention 94 vs pricing 36, explicitly flagged not-priced. Continuous glucose monitoring is the infrastructure layer of the shift from episodic treatment to continuous measurement, and it is a GLP-1 complement rather than a victim. Pricing 50 with gap 12 understates a decade of demographic volume.

Pricing 44, gap 14, opportunity 58. Named as a beneficiary in two separate multi-year claims at 0.65 and 0.80 confidence. Gas is the marginal AI fuel and data-center gas procurement is moving from spot to contracted — that converts a commodity producer into an infrastructure annuity, which the pricing does not reflect.

Pricing 30 with opportunity 60 and gap 15, and no theme attached — which is why it's mispriced. It is a direct beneficiary of the 5% regime (investment float income), of auto financing stress pushing buyers to optimize total cost of ownership, and of rising physical-risk repricing. Short-duration, cash-generative, clears the hurdle rate on today's earnings.

Pricing 30, gap 23. Named explicitly in the briefs as the poster child for AI seat-pricing punishment. That is now the consensus view and it is in the price; the asymmetry is that Adobe holds the professional creative distribution channel through which agentic generation must be commercialised. Contrarian, not high-confidence.

Pricing 38 vs the cybersecurity theme's pricing of 67 — the cheapest way to own the highest-conviction non-discretionary tax in the book. Zero-trust architecture is exactly what enterprises buy when they restrict external AI models over data-exfiltration fear, which happened in the observation set this month.

Pricing 20, gap 26, no theme. The GLP-1 bear case is fully priced into staples; what is not priced is that fuel-driven substitution toward home consumption and value retail (Walmart raise, Kroger, restaurant slowdown at Darden) routes volume back through packaged food and beverage. A 5% discount rate also re-rates reliable cash yield.

Named as a beneficiary in two separate data-center power claims (0.65 and 0.80 confidence). Pricing 57 is not cheap, but it monetises the scarcest input in the entire thesis — skilled mechanical and electrical trades — and the market still models it as a cyclical contractor rather than the labour chokepoint of the AI buildout.

Pricing 25, gap 32. The in-home consolidation of entertainment (Visa: more cards pay for streaming than cinema and concerts combined) plus fuel-constrained mobility routes youth attention and spend into virtual venues. Speculative, but the pricing implies none of it.

Pricing 24, gap 19, no theme assigned. Edge inference migrating to devices and agents making autonomous network calls both raise the value of the connectivity layer; meanwhile it is a cash-generative, short-duration compounder in a 5% world. Unloved and structurally advantaged.

anti_theses: 'The housing shortage is an investable long thesis.' It is a real shortage and an uninvestable trade: trend 22, narrative 15, contract signings -4.7%, builders cutting price rather than volume, 58% of markets in seller surplus. Demand is rationed by monthly payment, and construction robotics will not change labour cost this cycle. Own the repair-and-stay-put MRO expression instead.

'Nuclear is the answer to AI power demand.' Directionally right, temporally wrong. Every observed procurement decision this month went to gas and on-site generation — Meta's seven plants, Amazon's $8B generators, Mitsui's LNG. Nuclear's 5-20 year horizon is the worst possible duration profile against a 5.44% 30-year.

'China revenue is recovery optionality for Western AI semis.' Huawei's Ascend 960 on a Q1 2027 timetable plus rare-earth leverage at the summit means the correct model is structurally zero. Anyone underwriting NVDA/AMD with a China reversion line is double-counting.

'AI capex demand will break and take the power trade with it.' The financing structure is circular (Nvidia into Anthropic, vendor-linked cloud commitments), so the unwind is a capital-structure event. But the generation, transmission and interconnect assets contracted along the way are long-lived and multi-tenant. Distinguish the equity of second-tier AI capex from the electrons.

'Rates revert to 3% and the levered consumer/housing/REIT complex re-rates.' With $365tn of global debt and sovereigns competing at every auction, term premium stays elevated. The 5% cost of money is the regime. Businesses whose only moat was cheap capital do not get bailed out by duration.

'GLP-1 is the durable health trade.' It is a maturing share war — Novo's rebrand and strategic 'rethinking' is the tell, and theme pricing (61) already exceeds trend (60). The unpriced leg of the same human shift is devices, procedures and continuous monitoring: attention 94, pricing 36.

'Humanoid robots are a near-term consumer market.' Search interest in 'humanoid robot price' and a 5,000-unit Optimus order are status and procurement signals, not economics. Robotics pricing at 58 versus trend 45 says the narrative is ahead of the order book by years.

'AI kills all incumbent software.' It kills seat pricing, not distribution. Copilot at 30M seats shows the incumbent with the channel wins; the casualties are standalone model vendors and per-seat suites that cannot reprice to outcomes.

'Travel and experiences recover as consumers prioritize memories over things.' At $107 crude the operator cannot sell the experience profitably — Ryanair cutting winter capacity, NCLH near lows, Darden slowing, MGM's takeover collapsing. Desire is intact; unit economics are not.

'Value retail is the safe consumer trade.' Narrative 77 against trend 38. Everyone owns the trade-down story, and when everyone owns it the margin gets competed away — Kroger already showed softer sales.
what_would_change: Interconnect queues shortening materially or a policy fast-track for grid connection — that would relieve the power constraint and compress the premium on behind-the-meter generation and contractors.

A hyperscaler cutting or deferring committed capex on a financing (not demand) trigger, or an Anthropic/OpenAI-linked funding failure — it would validate the circular-financing risk and de-rate the whole physical AI supply chain for 2-4 quarters even though electron demand persists.

The 30-year falling decisively below 4% with credible fiscal consolidation — that resurrects long-duration themes (nuclear, space, longevity, housing) and undermines the short-duration/hard-asset tilt.
Crude and diesel normalising below $70/$4 — that releases the household budget, revives out-of-home leisure and travel, and weakens the energy-security-as-consumer-need shift.

Evidence that agents transact at scale — Meta Muse or an equivalent generating measurable merchant take-rate — would convert the advertising re-plumbing hypothesis from speculative to consensus and force an upgrade of TTD/APP/META and a downgrade of legacy e-commerce take-rates.
A named enterprise publishing audited headcount reduction attributable to agentic software would re-rate outcome-priced AI tools and accelerate the collapse of seat-based pricing.
Robotic-surgery procedure volumes and device order books confirming the 107% search surge in reported results — that converts medical-devices from an attention signal into a flow signal.
A US-China détente returning accelerator export licences — low probability, but it would invalidate the 'model China to zero' stance.
Mortgage rates below 5.5% with inventory absorption — that would revive turnover-linked consumption and invalidate the repair-and-stay-put expression of the housing thesis.
A major grid or cyber failure at a data center scale — it would step-change the security premium and pull forward years of resilience spend into a single budget cycle.
